title: observability: token-kv metrics + cost/latency dashboards + alert tuning
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-token KV cache behavior and the associated cost/latency impact. This PR surfaces token-level KV hit/miss and per-token cost + latency breakdowns, standardizes tracing spans for serving pipeline steps, and adjusts alert thresholds to reduce noise while preserving SLO coverage. Changes are backwards compatible: metrics are additive namespaced under redwood.token.*, dashboards are additive Grafana JSON, and alerts are tuned but not removed. Includes integration tests and migration notes.

What I changed (high level): added token-level KV metrics (hits, misses, eviction counts, hit latency histogram), introduced per-token cost/latency aggregation (avg/p50/p95/p99), standardized tracing spans for cache_lookup, batch_scheduler, model_infer, and added a Grafana dashboard JSON + updated alert rules. Tuned several alerts to use rate() + longer evaluation windows to reduce flapping.

Rollout plan: feature gated by env var REDWOOD_TOKEN_OBSERVABILITY=false by default. Gradual rollout: enable for 10% of serving nodes -> 50% -> 100% over 48h while monitoring new metric volumes and cost. Alerts initially set to informational for first 24h.

Backward compatibility / migration: no breaking API changes. Operators should import the new Grafana JSON and update alert manager rules; note added cardinality for token labels (we cap tokenized prompt length label to avoid high cardinality). See docs/observability/token_metrics.md for fine-grained guidance.
